main_result.description: For successful execution of the deposit source model with its configured Lido withdrawal pipeline, the actual Lido and beacon calls preserve pointwise ETH accounting from Lido to beacon and restore the router balance. A nonempty successful run derives the configured 32-ether per-key amount from these effects. Full physical prefix and metadata correspondence remains open. The physical-metadata executor also derives the packed uint64 timestamp/block writes and preserved upper fields before its actual withdrawal/beacon continuation, including the zero-key event and failing-root rollback.
main_result.model: Source transaction interpreter with source-interpreted Lido withdrawal, raw beacon calls and Verity physical contract storage; allocation/module prefix and metadata remain partial; additional physical metadata executor consumes those writes before the same live suffix

theorems.name: LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PDeposit1.actual_live_pipeline_conservation
theorems.doc:
/-- Successful modeled deposit execution preserves pointwise ETH accounting
from Lido to beacon. A nonempty success derives the configured 32-ether amount
from the actual withdrawal/beacon calls and the final router balance assertion.
It assumes only the existing source pipeline binding and distinct roles shown
below; no funding, prepared transcript, capacity or per-key amount premise. -/
theorems.statement:
theorem actual_live_pipeline_conservation (k : Queue.Keccak) (config : Pipeline.Config)
    (staticOther : StaticCall.External) (other : Live.External)
    (ctx : RouterDeposit.Context) (inputs : RouterDeposit.Inputs)
    (before after : World) (attempts : List Live.Attempt)
    (bound : Pipeline.Bound config inputs.liveContext before.live)
    (lido_ne_router : inputs.liveContext.self ≠ inputs.liveContext.sender)
    (router_ne_beacon : inputs.liveContext.sender ≠ beaconAddress ctx)
    (h : execute (Pipeline.external k config staticOther other) ctx inputs before =
      ⟨.ok (), after, attempts⟩) :
    ∃ prepared transcript,
      prepareDepositABI inputs.layout inputs.storage inputs.oracle inputs.config
        inputs.requested before.allocationTranscript inputs.moduleId inputs.limits
        inputs.obtainDepositData DEPOSIT_SIZE = (.ok prepared, transcript) ∧
      CallSpec.Balances before.live.balances after.live.balances
        inputs.liveContext.self (beaconAddress ctx) (prepared.values.actualKeys * DEPOSIT_SIZE) ∧
      (prepared.values.actualKeys = 0 ∨ inputs.config.maxEBType1.val = DEPOSIT_SIZE)

theorems.name: LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PDeposit1.actual_physical_metadata_before_calls
theorems.doc:
/-- The computed preparation updates the physical module word and source event
before the actual withdrawal/beacon continuation. The prefix world is consumed
by that continuation, including the zero-key case. This does not replace the
open allocation/module CALL or deployment/configuration composition. -/
theorems.statement:
theorem actual_physical_metadata_before_calls (hash : Keccak) (callee : Live.External) (ctx : RouterDeposit.Context)
    (inputs : RouterDeposit.Inputs) (before after : World) (attempts : List Live.Attempt)
    (h : execute hash callee ctx inputs before = ⟨.ok (),after,attempts⟩) :
    ∃ credentials prepared transcript,
      prepareDepositABI inputs.layout inputs.storage inputs.oracle inputs.config
        inputs.requested before.allocationTranscript inputs.moduleId inputs.limits
        inputs.obtainDepositData DEPOSIT_SIZE = (.ok prepared,transcript) ∧
      after.allocationTranscript = transcript ∧
      let updated := update hash ctx inputs.liveContext.sender prepared before.live
      let key := moduleDepositSlot hash prepared.moduleId
      let packed := (updated.core.readContractSlot inputs.liveContext.sender.val key).val
      (packed % 2^64 = before.live.core.blockTimestamp.val % 2^64 ∧
       packed / 2^64 % 2^64 = before.live.core.blockNumber.val % 2^64 ∧
       packed / 2^128 = (before.live.core.readContractSlot inputs.liveContext.sender.val key).val / 2^128) ∧
      updated.balances = before.live.balances ∧
      updated.logs = before.live.logs ++ [routerEvent inputs.liveContext.sender prepared] ∧
      ((prepared.values.actualKeys = 0 ∧ after.live = updated ∧ attempts = []) ∨
       (prepared.values.actualKeys ≠ 0 ∧ Nonempty
         (LiveBeaconCommitted.SuffixCommitment callee ctx inputs.liveContext credentials prepared
           updated after.live attempts)))

theorems.name: LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PDeposit1.actual_physical_metadata_failure_restores
theorems.doc:
/-- A failing execution restores this physical metadata together with the
whole live world, using the existing declared root rollback semantics. -/
theorems.statement:
theorem actual_physical_metadata_failure_restores (hash : Keccak) (callee : Live.External) (ctx : RouterDeposit.Context)
    (inputs : RouterDeposit.Inputs) (before after : World) (fault : LiveBeacon.Fault)
    (attempts : List Live.Attempt)
    (h : execute hash callee ctx inputs before = ⟨.error fault,after,attempts⟩) :
    after = before

covered: The root success derives authorization, executed preparation, the actual withdrawal and the beacon-loop effects in the same live world.

The withdrawal derives available funding and precise debit/credit from success of the called source pipeline. Arbitrary fallback behavior is retained and proved unreachable on the covered getter/receiver routes.

The final router assertion equates the actual Lido withdrawal with the beacon-loop debit, yielding pointwise conservation and maxEBType1 = 32 ether for nonempty success. No funding, prepared-result, per-key amount or callee-preservation premise is supplied. Zero-key success is included.

PhysicalMetadata.execute consumes the computed preparation, writes both uint64 fields at the actual mapping slot plus one (with uint256 wrap), preserves both upper configuration fields, and emits the semantic router event before zero return or the actual withdrawal/beacon continuation. A failed root restores these physical effects. No successful sub-stage, count restriction or caller metadata premise is supplied.
missing: The allocation/module prefix still reads supplied storage/oracle/transcript inputs and an obtainDepositData outcome, rather than the physical live-world module call. Its source guards, ABI, values and consumed state need complete correspondence.

The physical metadata-before-call executor is now registered, but its full composition with the earlier pipeline-conservation result still requires deriving the configuration binding at the updated same live world. The earlier LiveBeacon.execute retains its historical auxiliary metadata. The actual module-call prefix and deployed LOG topics/data are not established by the new executor.

The public facade covers the declared source executor. Actual outer ABI/error bytes and complete observable failure/rollback correspondence remain to be connected. Its supplementary model rollback is not claimed as full Solidity rollback.
conditions: A successful execution of LiveBeacon.execute with the concrete Pipeline.external source dispatchers. The existing Pipeline.Bound links locator and consensus reads, separates queue/oracle/locator roles, and requires their code to be present in the entry world.
The Lido and router roles are distinct, and router and beacon roles are distinct. These remain explicit runtime/configuration facts, not invariants established by this increment.

Source functions and model inputs retain their declared interpretation. The static external interpreter and arbitrary fallback are universally quantified; no new preservation condition on the fallback is imposed.

The physical-metadata result quantifies over its own computed root execution and arbitrary live callees with no additional success, packing or configuration premise. The inherited prepared allocation/module prefix and source Context remain explicit model inputs; their physical source connection is not claimed. Keccak is the existing opaque primitive applied to the two actual mapping ABI words.
outside: General compiler correctness, the declared Verity semantics, cryptographic primitives, general gas and consensus retain their accepted boundaries. No stronger source/ABI/storage/call premise is hidden in them.
The historical abstract/Verity theorem pair remains separate model evidence and is not required to equal this source executor.

theorems.name: LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PDeposit1.source_deposit_conserves_and_rolls_back
theorems.doc:
/--
Commit-branch-explicit conservation, and rollback of the deployments that
would break it, for the SRv3 deposit push at
`lidofinance/core@17005714f151e5502c559932319a3f2f74ac2436`:

* `contracts/0.8.25/sr/StakingRouter.sol`, `deposit`, lines 942--997;
* `contracts/0.4.24/Lido.sol`, `withdrawDepositableEther`, lines 869--886;
* `contracts/0.4.24/Lido.sol`, `_spendDepositableEther`, lines 839--859;
* `contracts/0.8.25/lib/BeaconChainDepositor.sol`,
  `makeBeaconChainDeposits32ETH`, lines 36--64.

Two conjuncts, one per half of the guarantee wording; neither is definitional.

*Conservation.* On the committed-push branch -- the only branch that moves wei
-- the wei pulled from Lido at line 983 equals the wei pushed to the beacon
deposit contract by the loop at `BeaconChainDepositor.sol` lines 53--63, and
the two independently written source formulas agree: line 972's
`depositsValue = actualDepositsCount * MAX_EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_WC_TYPE_01` and
the loop's `pushedValue`.  This is exactly the invariant the `assert` at line
996 checks, and it is proved from the source-shaped guard structure, not
assumed: `committedDeposits` carries arbitrary `Nat`s, and only the assert
gate forces the equality.  The claim is deliberately restricted to the
committed branch because `Outcome.pulled`/`Outcome.pushed` are defined as `0`
on every other branch, so a whole-path accessor equality would be mostly
`0 = 0`.  The kill-line
`LidoSRv3.Tests.DepositVectors.dropped_conservation_assert_breaks_pulled_eq_pushed`
shows this conjunct is load-bearing: dropping the line 996 assert branch from
`run` (`SolidityDeposit.mutantRun`) lets a skewed deployment commit with
`pulled ≠ pushed`.

*Rollback.* A deployment whose `MAX_EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_WC_TYPE_01`
(`StakingRouter.sol` line 65) differs from `DEPOSIT_SIZE`
(`BeaconChainDepositor.sol` line 24) never commits a mismatched push: on any
nonempty key batch the whole transaction reverts -- the failing line 996
`assert` is a Solidity 0.8 `Panic(0x01)`, and the pinned span contains no
`try`/`catch` and no failure-swallowing low-level call.  This is the
source-plane rollback content, and it is not definitional either: it needs the
empty-batch early return at line 978 excluded (`committedNoDeposits`) and the
assert gate to exclude a mismatched commit (`committed_implies_conserving`).

Caveats, stated rather than hidden:

* The abstract-transaction rollback fact used in earlier revisions --
  `observation` maps a reverting outcome to `.reverted`, whose
  `committedState`/`committedTrace` are `before`/`⟨[], [], []⟩` by definition
  (`A-ABSTRACT-TX`) -- is definitional in this model and is therefore *not* a
  conjunct of this registered parent.  It remains available as the
  unregistered child `revert_restores_state_value_and_logs` (and
  `SolidityDeposit.reverting_outcome_rolls_back`).
* Conservation on the commit branch holds without a `ConservingConfig`
  hypothesis only because the line 996 `assert` is modelled as the revert it
  is; `SolidityDeposit.pulled_eq_pushed_iff_conserving` shows the pull and
  push scales agree *exactly when* the deployment sets them equal.
* Arithmetic is read as unbounded `Nat` (`A-SOURCE-SHAPED`): truncating `Nat`
  division matches EVM `DIV`, but no overflow reasoning is performed.
* Locator-derived DSM authentication at lines 943 and 1173--1179 remains an
  interface fact outside this data-only model, so this is not a claim about
  every possible caller.
-/
theorems.statement:
theorem source_deposit_conserves_and_rolls_back
    (cfg : SourceDepositConfig) (inp : SourceDepositInput) :
    CommittedPushConserves cfg inp ∧ NonConservingDeploymentReverts cfg inp

theorems.name: LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PDeposit1.actual_deposit_call_slot_success_and_revert
theorems.doc:
/-- Retains the prior complete suffix statement and additionally consumes an
executed allocation, after physical admission, before the module CALL. Available
ether, static-oracle realization and phase cursor/config provenance remain open. -/
theorems.statement:
theorem actual_deposit_call_slot_success_and_revert
    (q : StaticCall.External) (locator : Live.Address) (cursor : Live.Word)
    (m w : Live.External) (ctx : RouterDeposit.Context) (liveCtx : Live.Context)
    (i : ModuleCall.Input) (before : Live.World) :
    (let result := DepositDsmCall.execute q locator cursor depositPhysicalKeccak m w ctx liveCtx i before;
      match result.outcome with
      | .ok _ => DepositDsmCall.Effects q locator cursor depositPhysicalKeccak m w ctx liveCtx i before
          result.world result.attempts result.locatorAttempts
      | .error _ => result.world = before) ∧
    (∀ (oracle : TrioAlloc1.StaticOracle) (cfg : TrioAlloc1.Config) (available : TrioAlloc1.Word),
      DepositAllocation.Effects q locator cursor depositPhysicalKeccak oracle cfg available m w ctx liveCtx i before
        (DepositAllocation.execute q locator cursor depositPhysicalKeccak oracle cfg available m w ctx liveCtx i before) ∧
      DepositAllocation.AllocationFailureStops q locator cursor depositPhysicalKeccak oracle cfg available
        m w ctx liveCtx i before)

assumptions.risk: The external callees reached by the modeled Lido, StakingRouter and gateway executions -- module obtainDepositData bodies, the beacon deposit contract, the EIP-7251 consolidation-request predeploy, the WithdrawalQueue finalization callback and the configured refund recipient -- do not call back into Lido, the router or the gateway. `LidoSRv3/Audit/Source/NoReentry.lean` names this on the Live external-call interpreter as `NoReentry (external : External) (self : List Address)`: a call targeting a protected address is rejected, an accepted reply returns a world agreeing with the received world on every protected address (all storage words and the balance), and no recorded nested attempt into a protected address was accepted. A callee that re-enters (for example a malicious module implementation or a refund recipient that calls back into the gateway) is not covered.
assumptions.justification: Thomas 2026-09-17 (step 1b of the "not proven" cleanup): the deployed callees are audited protocol contracts, the beacon deposit contract and an EIP predeploy, so their non-re-entry may be assumed rather than proved per body. The registry prose at `audit/topup-call-history/README.md:51` argued that adding a `noReentry` premise would not close the TOPUP-2 per-block cap; the owner overrides that reading for the five rows below, where the premise constrains only the callee interpreter of theorems that already thread the exact returned world, and where the corollaries are stated on those theorems. Corollaries: `PDeposit1NoReentry.actual_physical_metadata_conserves_no_reentry` (DEPOSIT-1 ledger plus `Confined other [lido, router]`), `PTopup1NoReentry.actual_continuation_locator_conserves_no_reentry` (TOPUP-1), `PReserve1NoReentry.actual_reserve_history_final_reserve` (RESERVE-1: the final reserve word equals the spending stage's), `PConsolidationEth1NoReentry.settlement_preserves_gateway_and_vault_storage` (ETH-1: gateway and vault storage equal the post-quota storage after the inbox and refund CALLs) and `PAddress1NoReentry.claim_returns_committed_storage` / `actual_claim_batch_no_reentry` (ADDRESS-1: the claimed bit and locked-ether write survive the recipient CALL; no accepted nested call into the queue). The generic consequences for `Live.call` are `call_storage`, `call_balance`, `call_self_rejected` and `call_nested_rejects`.
assumptions.violation_impact: If a callee re-enters Lido, the router or the gateway, the corollaries above do not apply: the final reserve, the gateway/vault storage after settlement, the claimed bit after a recipient CALL and the confinement of module/beacon calls are no longer derived, and the exact-returned-world parents must be consulted with the re-entrant world.
assumptions.validation: `lake build LidoSRv3.Audit.Source.NoReentry LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PDeposit1NoReentry LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PTopup1NoReentry LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PReserve1NoReentry LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PConsolidationEth1NoReentry LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PAddress1NoReentry` checks the corollaries. The premise itself is validated only by review of the pinned callee sources (NodeOperatorsRegistry/CSM obtainDepositData, deposit_contract.sol, the EIP-7251 predeploy, WithdrawalQueue.finalize, the refund recipient configuration); it is not proved for the deployed runtimes.
assumptions.removal_path: Prove `NoReentry` for each deployed callee body: model obtainDepositData of NOR/CSM, the beacon deposit contract, the EIP-7251 predeploy and WithdrawalQueue.finalize as Live executables and show they issue no CALL into Lido, the router or the gateway; bind the refund recipient configuration. Then replace the premise by those theorems in the five corollaries.

model_not_deployment: These are proofs about a model, not about a deployed contract.
The subject is a Lean model of Staking Router v3, written against pinned source lidofinance/core@17005714f151e5502c559932319a3f2f74ac2436.

No theorem here binds to deployed bytecode, a runtime codehash, a constructor, or a chain address. The SRv3 contracts are deployed on mainnet with lidofinance/core v4.0.0 (2026-07-24; StakingRouter proxy 0xFdDf38947aFB03C621C71b06C9C70bce73f12999, TopUpGateway proxy 0x3FC2C71579D80790Aaa3fc7Be8B66ac39dC57374); the theorems still speak about the model, not about that deployment.
CHECKED means *the named Lean theorem builds*. It does not mean audited, verified on chain, or closed.

CHECKED is conditional, and one gap has no theorem to compose. Every row is proved under named premises — the named-premises table below gives them per row, and A-SHA256-FFI and A-EIP4788-AUTHENTIC are HIGH severity.
